question: Describe continuous spectrum, emission line spectrum and absorption line spectrum. Explain why an atomic spectrum is useful in identifying the element producing it.

options.A: A continuous spectrum has bright lines on a dark background. An emission line spectrum has dark lines on a bright background. An atomic spectrum cannot identify an element.
options.B: A continuous spectrum is an unbroken range of wavelengths. An emission line spectrum consists of bright lines on a dark background from excited atoms, while an absorption line spectrum consists of dark lines on a continuous bright background when a cooler gas absorbs selected wavelengths. Because each element has a characteristic set of spectral lines, its spectrum can identify it.
options.C: All three spectra contain exactly the same continuous wavelengths, so spectral lines cannot distinguish elements.
options.D: Absorption lines are caused by emission from hot solids, and emission lines are caused by white light passing through a cold gas.
